chapter: The Original Dixieland band to California
title: Banned from San Francisco for six months
summary: The local union business agent barred the band for not depositing transfer cards; they played non-union jobs in Oakland and Joe left for Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: No. That was long before I went to Seattle. Well, it wasn't that long. I went to Seattle in '28. But I came back... What caused all the trouble was, we
did not put the transfer in.
Oh, yes, I'm sorry, I interrupted you.

So when we got to that radio station, the San Francisco Local had got wind of it. And there was a business agent who said, "Where are you guys from? If you're from out of town, you deposit your transfer card." We said, "no." "Well, you can't play."

We hadn't even started. He said, "You cannot play on this radio and you cannot play in this jurisdiction for six months. And if you think that you're going to get wise, then you'll get suspended from the whole Federation."
So what did you do for work, for employment?
So we came over to Oakland and played some non-union jobs. But we couldn't play in San Francisco.
In other words, San Francisco and Oakland were two different...

Oh, two different locals, yes. And Oakland wasn't nearly as strict... San Francisco, like I said, was the strictest union in the United States. So I hung around there and wasn't doing nothin'. And I says, "To heck with this deal. I'm going back to Los Angeles." So me and the trombone player and Victor Spencer came back down
